clue.text: Horse-drawn vehicle mostly conveying peasant?

indicators.note: conveying means carrying something within, so one piece sits inside the other
mostly means the word loses its final letter here

parts.note: early trams were pulled by horses along rails
an oik is British slang for a coarse, low-class person, a loose stand-in for a peasant

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn carriage spends most of its time ferrying a country labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse-drawn trams once ran on city streets; 'mostly' leaves TRA. Oik is British slang for an uncouth, low-class person, and the whole clue also pictures a Russian sleigh carrying a peasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian carriage or sleigh drawn by three horses abreast, which might well carry a muzhik.

clue.text: Strike, a course of action restricting hospital workers primarily

indicators.note: restricting means holding something in, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: a tack is a course of action or approach, as in 'try a different tack'
H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

indicators.note: primarily asks for just the opening letter of workers

explanation.surface: A trade union plan to strike that limits what hospital staff can do.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwack is to hit hard with a heavy blow, a synonym of strike.

clue.text: Construction of sort you do not fit for buildings?

indicators.note: construction means building something up anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Builders complain that some piece of work is unsuitable for the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: someone who loves fresh air and open country is not suited to being shut indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: An outdoorsy type prefers open air to the inside of houses, playfully described as unfit for buildings.

clue.text: Some think Armageddon is just fate

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Certain people believe the end of the world is simply destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Karma, in Hindu and Buddhist thought, is the destiny you earn by your deeds, so it is just fate.

clue.text: Natural key in "Kind of Blue", eschewing runs in various styles

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
eschewing means avoiding, so a letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: electric blue is a shade of blue (the quotes play on the Miles Davis album)
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
C major is the key with no sharps or flats, all naturals on the piano

explanation.surface: A jazz fan describes a piece in the style of the Miles Davis album that avoids fast passages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eschewing' removes R from ELECTRIC, leaving ELECTIC, and 'in' places C inside it. The quoted album title tempts you to think of jazz modes, but it simply gives a shade of blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclectic means drawing on many sources or styles, so it fits doing something in various styles.

clue.text: Constabulary is corrupt; prison officer commanding uprightly is a rarity

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading upright means from the bottom up, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
taken as written
to rot is to decay or corrupt
a cell is where a prisoner is held
OC is the military abbreviation for officer commanding

explanation.surface: A scandal: the police force is rotten, and a jail governor is running things on the straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprightly' turns the whole chain MET IS ROT CELL OC, read from the bottom of the light upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A collector's item is something scarce and sought after, so it is a rarity.

clue.text: European association involves absolutely all the people

parts.note: very and absolutely both act as intensifiers, as in 'the very best'
a body is an organised group or association

explanation.surface: A European organisation includes every single citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: Everybody means every person, all the people together.

clue.text: Wavy line in Spanish lake, amid change in water level

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the letter is placed inside

parts.note: a tide is the regular rise and fall of the sea
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A ripple on a Spanish lake while the water level shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish lake' looks like a unit, but 'in Spanish' belongs with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilde is the wavy mark over the n in Spanish words like 'mañana'.

clue.text: Sloppy embrace in which love loses heart

indicators.note: in which says the next piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a caress is a gentle loving touch, close to an embrace

indicators.note: loses heart means the middle letters of the word are removed

explanation.surface: A sloppy hug in which the passion fades away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses heart' leaves the outer letters of love, and 'in which' sets them in the middle of the embrace. Love here is a feeling, not tennis zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless work is sloppy, done without attention to detail.

clue.text: I'm no blue insect fluttering like a firefly

indicators.note: fluttering suggests wings moving about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A firefly protests that it is not some blue bug flitting about.
explanation.definitionFit: Bioluminescent describes a living thing that makes its own light, as fireflies do.

clue.text: There may be a race to supply one desire spanning an interval

definitions.text: There may be a race to supply one

indicators.note: spanning means stretching across, so the other letters sit inside

parts.note: will means wish or desire
an gives the letter A
a term is a fixed period or interval of time

explanation.surface: A runner's wish to compete stretched over a period of time.
explanation.walkthrough: A race here is a millrace, the channel carrying water to turn a mill wheel, not a running contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A millrace is the stream feeding a water-driven mill, so such a mill may have one supplying it.

clue.text: Half the Continent embraces the French mathematician

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so one piece goes inside
Half means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: to Britons, the Continent means mainland Europe
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Half of Europe takes to its heart a French mathematician.
explanation.walkthrough: To British setters 'the Continent' means mainland Europe; 'Half' keeps its first three letters, and 'embraces' wraps them round the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was an eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician of enormous output.

clue.text: Start to croon nothings?

indicators.note: start to asks for the opening letter of croon

parts.note: each nothing is a zero, shaped like the letter O, so two give OO

explanation.surface: A lover begins to murmur sweet nothings.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: to coo is to start murmuring sweet nothings.
explanation.definitionFit: To coo is to murmur softly and lovingly, which is how sweet nothings are crooned.

clue.text: River in winding valley, water source that's fine as far as it goes

definitions.text: fine as far as it goes

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another
winding means twisting about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
a well is a source of water drawn from the ground

explanation.surface: A river snaking through a valley and a spring make a pleasant landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' turns VALLEY into ALLVEY, and 'in' puts R inside it to make ALLVERY.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'all very well' grants that something is acceptable up to a point, with reservations.

clue.text: Weight the queen added to overthrow of king, perhaps

indicators.note: overthrow means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a king is one example of a playing card
HM stands for Her Majesty, the queen

explanation.surface: A heavy matter: the queen joined in the toppling of a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrow of' turns CARD into DRAC. The royal surface makes you think of revolution, but the king is a playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: A drachm is an old unit of weight, an eighth of an apothecaries' ounce.

clue.text: Guevara and Trotsky enlisting American person who's changeable

indicators.note: enlisting means taking on as a recruit, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
Leon Trotsky, the Russian revolutionary

explanation.surface: Two revolutionaries recruit a Yank who keeps switching sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A chameleon, literally a colour-changing lizard, is figuratively a person who changes views to suit the moment.

clue.text: Most of old city photos will show hot spots

indicators.note: most of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad
pics is informal for photos

explanation.surface: Holiday snaps of an ancient city show sun-baked places.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are the hot regions either side of the equator, so hot spots in a broad sense.

clue.text: Dogmatist that is harbouring awfully loud ego

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering inside, so the other letters go within
awfully means badly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dogmatic person, that is one with a big noisy self-regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' scrambles 'loud ego' into a seven-letter run that 'harbouring' tucks between the two letters of the Latin abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideologue is a rigid adherent of a doctrine, a dogmatist.

clue.text: Soprano's initial exercises going through hums and unvoiced words

indicators.note: going through means passing inside, so these letters sit within

parts.note: a whir is a steady humming sound

indicators.note: initial asks for the first letter of Soprano's

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercises

explanation.surface: A singer's warm-up routine runs through humming and quiet mouthing.
explanation.definitionFit: Whispers are words spoken without vibrating the vocal cords, so unvoiced.

clue.text: Constable's subject to hearing what might have got cowboy actor's attention

indicators.note: to hearing says the words are judged by how they sound

parts.words: what might have got cowboy actor's attention
parts.note: a call of 'Hey, Wayne!' would catch John Wayne's notice

explanation.surface: A policeman's suspect shouted for a Western star.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable is John Constable, the English landscape painter, not a police officer. 'Hey, Wayne' sounds like the painting's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hay Wain is John Constable's famous 1821 painting of a hay cart in a river.

clue.text: Cardinal, say, framing endless paean in verse?

indicators.note: framing means surrounding, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: cardinal red is a shade, so a cardinal suggests the colour red

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a paean is a song of praise, a hymn

explanation.surface: A churchman gives a song of praise without finishing it, perhaps in poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The cardinal is a colour, not a prelate; 'endless' clips the song of praise to HYM and 'framing' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rhymed is written with rhyming lines, so it is in verse.

clue.text: Brilliant figure getting promotion over delinquent youth

indicators.note: promotion means moving up, and in a down clue going up reverses the word

parts.note: fig. is the abbreviation for figure, as in a book's illustrations
a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth gang member

explanation.surface: A bright young offender is raised to a higher rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting promotion' raises FIG upward in the down light, giving GIF. Teddy boys were a 1950s British youth subculture.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifted means exceptionally talented, a synonym of brilliant.

clue.text: Argentine worker maybe agitating vs Hitlerism

indicators.note: agitating means stirring up, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A labourer in Buenos Aires campaigns against fascism.
explanation.walkthrough: Argentine here means made of silver (argent), not from Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: A silversmith works in silver, which heraldry and old usage call argent, so an argentine worker.

clue.text: Shooter who competes in winter Olympics?

definitions.meaning: a luge competitor rides a small sled feet first down an ice track

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a classic German handgun and a person who races on a luge sled.

clue.text: Peace briefly being interrupted by radio telephony is a pain

indicators.note: being interrupted by means another piece breaks into this one
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: hush means quiet, peace
RT is the abbreviation for radio telephony

explanation.surface: A quiet moment broken by a radio message is annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' clips the call for quiet to HUS, and 'being interrupted by' breaks it open for the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that hurts causes pain, so it is a pain in the sense of being painful.

clue.text: Band of flowers taking field over, escaping borders

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the remaining letters are read backwards
escaping borders means the first and last letters of field are lost

explanation.surface: A ring of blooms taking over a meadow, spilling past its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaping borders' leaves IEL from FIELD, and 'over' turns it round. 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers worn around the neck.

clue.text: Ecstasy par golfer's regularly missing?

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: regularly missing drops every other letter, keeping the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A golfer who keeps missing par finds bliss anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a player usually off the par score may be in ecstasy at scoring two under for once.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle in golf is a hole played two strokes under par, a thrill for any golfer.

clue.text: Flower of the old British in rowing team

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
ye is an archaic form of the

explanation.surface: A bloom of the British past wears the colours of a rowing crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wild flower once used to treat eye complaints.

clue.text: Pairs finishing last are running with stamina

indicators.note: pairs finishing asks for the final two letters of each following word

explanation.surface: Pairs finishing at the back are still running, and with real endurance.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the last pair of letters from last, are, running and with: ST, RE, NG, TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Strength in the sense of staying power is a synonym of stamina.

clue.text: Apparently half-cut duke offers port

indicators.note: half-cut means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: ostensibly means apparently, on the face of it

explanation.surface: A seemingly tipsy aristocrat offers a glass of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' keeps OSTEN from OSTENSIBLY. Half-cut is British slang for tipsy, and port is the drink; here it is a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostend is a Belgian seaport on the North Sea coast.
